subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Percentage: Finding the Whole, Percentage Increase and Decrease
seo_title: P6 Percentage Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers, PSLE Practice (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Finding the whole given a part and the percentage; finding percentage increase/decrease
meta_desc: Free P6 percentage practice: find the whole from a part, percentage increase and decrease, and PSLE word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The value before the change is always 100%.
key_sub: After a 20% discount you pay 80%: if 80% is $64, then 10% is $8 and 100% is $80.
body_html:
Percentage of a quantity

Per cent means “out of 100”. To find a percentage of a quantity, write the percentage as a fraction over 100 and multiply.

Example

Find 35% of 80.

35100 × 80 = 28.

Answer: 28

Finding the whole from a part

If you know a part and its percentage, find 1% (or 10%) first. Then find 100%.

Example

30% of a number is 45. What is the number?

30% → 45. 10% → 45 ÷ 3 = 15. 100% → 15 × 10 = 150.

Answer: 150

Percentage increase and decrease

The value before the change is always 100%.

To findDo this
percentage increaseincrease ÷ value before × 100%
percentage decreasedecrease ÷ value before × 100%
new value after a 25% increase125% of the value before
new value after a 20% decrease80% of the value before
Example

A price went up from $40 to $50. What is the percentage increase?

Increase = $10. $10$40 × 100% = 25%. Divide by $40 (before), not $50.

Answer: 25%

Before and after: price before a discount

When you know the value after the change, find what percentage it is of the value before.

Example

After a 20% discount, Siti paid $64. What was the usual price?

Usual price = 100% = 5 units. Paid = 80% = 4 units = $64. 1 unit = $16. 5 units = $80.

Answer: $80

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
30% of a number is 45, so the number is 30% of 45 = 13.5Find the whole: 10% = 15, so 100% = 150
40 to 50: 10 ÷ 50 = 20% increaseDivide by the value before: 10 ÷ 40 = 25%
Paid $64 after 20% off, so usual price = $64 + 20% of $64 = $76.80$64 is 80% of the usual price: 80% → $64, so 100% → $80
Ali has 25% more than Raju, so Raju has 25% less than AliCheck what is 100%: $75 is 25% more than $60, but $60 is 20% less than $75

faq.q: What is taught in P6 percentage?
faq.a: Primary 6 students find the whole when they know a part and its percentage, and work out percentage increase and decrease. They use these in PSLE word problems about discounts, enrolment, savings and “what percentage more”.

faq.q: How do I find the original price after a discount?
faq.a: Find what percentage you paid, then work back to 100%. After a 20% discount you pay 80%, so if 80% is $64, then 10% is $8 and 100% is $80.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in percentage increase and decrease?
faq.a: Dividing by the new value instead of the value before the change. From 40 to 50 is an increase of 10 ÷ 40 = 25%, not 10 ÷ 50 = 20%.

faq.q: Is percentage tested in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Percentage is part of the MOE Primary 6 syllabus and appears in both PSLE papers, often in multi-step word problems that use the model method.

items.q: The bar shows 60 split into 5 equal parts. What is 20% of 60?
items.e: 100% is 5 parts, so 20% is 1 part: 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Not 60 ÷ 20 = 3, and not 60 − 20 = 40. 48 is the other 80%.

items.q: The bar shows 84 split into 4 equal parts. What is 75% of 84?
items.e: 1 part is 25%: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. 75% is 3 parts: 3 × 21 = 63. 21 is only 25%. 112 comes from 84 ÷ 0.75, which is wrong here.

items.q: What is 30% of 45?
items.e: 30% of 45 = 30100 × 45 = 13.5. Multiply, do not divide: 150 would be the whole if 30% were 45. 31.5 is the other 70%.

items.q: What is 15% of 260?
items.e: 15% of 260 = 15100 × 260 = 39. 26 is only 10%. 221 is the other 85%. Do not take away 15.

items.q: What is 35% of 80?
items.e: 35% of 80 = 35100 × 80 = 28. 24 is only 30%. 52 is the other 65%. Do not take away 35.

items.q: What is 12% of 350?
items.e: 12% of 350 = 12100 × 350 = 42. 35 is only 10%. 308 is the other 88%.

items.q: What is 8% of 650?
items.e: 8% of 650 = 8100 × 650 = 52. 65 is 10%, not 8%. 598 is the other 92%.

items.q: What is 45% of 120?
items.e: 45% of 120 = 45100 × 120 = 54. 66 is the other 55%. 48 is only 40%.

items.q: What is 2.5% of 400?
items.e: 2.5% of 400 = 2.5100 × 400 = 10. 100 is 25%, not 2.5%. 1 is 0.25%.

items.q: What is 125% of 48?
items.e: 125% of 48 = 125100 × 48 = 60. 125% is more than the whole, so the answer is more than 48. 12 is only 25%. Do not add 125.

items.q: What is 60% of $75?
items.e: 60100 × $75 = $45. $30 is the other 40%. $7.50 is only 10%.

items.q: What is 15% of $36?
items.e: 15100 × $36 = $5.40. $3.60 is only 10%. $30.60 is the other 85%. Not $36 ÷ 15.

items.q: What is 40% of 2.5 kg? Give your answer in grams.
items.e: 2.5 kg = 2500 g. 40100 × 2500 g = 1000 g. 1500 g is the other 60%. 100 g comes from 2.5 kg = 250 g, but 1 kg = 1000 g.

items.q: What is 65% of 3 ℓ? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 3 ℓ = 3000 ml. 65100 × 3000 ml = 1950 ml. 1050 ml is the other 35%. Do not take away 65.

items.q: What is 20% of 1 h 30 min? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 1 h 30 min = 90 min, not 130 min. 20100 × 90 = 18 min. 72 min is the other 80%. 9 min is only 10%.

items.q: Which calculation gives 35% of 60?
items.e: 35% means 35100. So 35% of 60 = 35 ÷ 100 × 60 = 21. 60 ÷ 35 × 100 would find the whole if 35% were 60.

items.q: What percentage of 24 is 18?
items.e: 1824 = 75100 = 75%. 18% would be 18 out of 100. 25% is the other part.

items.q: Express 27 out of 60 as a percentage.
items.e: 2760 × 100% = 45%. 27% would be 27 out of 100. 55% is the other part. Do not take 27 from 60.

items.q: What percentage of 4 kg is 1.2 kg?
items.e: 1.24 = 0.3. 0.3 × 100% = 30%. 0.3% forgets to multiply by 100. 70% is the other part.

items.q: There are 40 students in a class. 35% of them wear glasses. How many students wear glasses?
items.e: 35100 × 40 = 14 students. 26 students do not wear glasses. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are only 40.

sets.title: Find the whole from a part (bar models)

items.q: The bar model shows that 30% of a number is 45. What is the number?
items.e: 30% → 45. 10% → 45 ÷ 3 = 15. 100% → 15 × 10 = 150. 13.5 is 30% of 45, which is the wrong question. 105 is the other 70%. Do not add 45 and 30.

items.q: The bar model shows that 25% of a number is 18. What is the number?
items.e: 25% → 18. 100% = 4 × 25%, so 100% → 4 × 18 = 72. 54 is only 75%. 4.5 is 25% of 18, which is the wrong question.

items.q: The bar model shows that 40% of a number is 56. What is the number?
The bar model shows that 60% of a number is 75. What is the number?
20% of a number is 14. What is the number?
15% of a number is 27. What is the number?
75% of a number is 96. What is the number?
12% of a number is 30. What is the number?
35% of a number is 63. What is the number?
5% of a number is 8. What is the number?
1% of a number is 3.5. What is the number?
120% of a number is 54. What is the number?
items.e: 120% → 54. 20% → 54 ÷ 6 = 9. 100% → 9 × 5 = 45. 120% is more than the whole, so the number is less than 54. 64.8 is 120% of 54. 43.2 takes 20% of 54 away, but 20% must be of the number, not of 54.

items.q: 40% of the mass of a bag of rice is 2.4 kg. What is the mass of the bag of rice?
items.e: 40% → 2.4 kg. 20% → 2.4 kg ÷ 2 = 1.2 kg. 100% → 1.2 kg × 5 = 6 kg. 0.96 kg is 40% of 2.4 kg. 3.6 kg is only 60%. 60 kg has the decimal point in the wrong place.

items.q: 80% of the cost of a book is $36. What is the cost of the book?
Ali spent 10% of his savings on a book. The book cost $6.50. How much were his savings?
30% of a number is 45. Which calculation gives the number?
25% of the beads in a box are red. There are 36 red beads. How many beads are there in the box?
items.e: 25% → 36. 100% = 4 × 25%, so 100% → 4 × 36 = 144. 9 is 25% of 36. 108 is the number of beads that are not red.

items.q: 45% of the students in a hall are boys. There are 27 boys. How many students are there in the hall?
items.e: 45% → 27. 5% → 27 ÷ 9 = 3. 100% → 3 × 20 = 60. 12.15 is 45% of 27. 33 is the number of girls, not all the students. Do not add 27 and 45.

items.q: Mei Ling spent 60% of her money and had $18 left. How much money did she have at first?
Hafiz used 35% of a bag of flour. He had 1.3 kg of flour left. How much flour was in the bag at first?
items.e: He had 100% − 35% = 65% left. 65% → 1.3 kg. 1% → 1.3 ÷ 65 = 0.02 kg. 100% → 2 kg. 1.755 kg adds 35% of 1.3 kg, but 35% is of the flour at first.

items.q: The model shows 40 increased by 25%. What is the new value?
items.e: 40 is 4 units, so 1 unit (25%) = 10. After the increase there are 5 units: 50. 10 is only the increase. Do not add 25.

items.q: Increase 80 by 15%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 15100 × 80 = 12. New value = 80 + 12 = 92. 12 is the increase, not the new value. Do not add 15.

items.q: Increase $250 by 8%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 8100 × $250 = $20. New value = $250 + $20 = $270. $20 is the increase. Do not add 8.

items.q: Increase 360 by 5%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 5100 × 360 = 18. New value = 360 + 18 = 378. 18 is the increase. 342 is a decrease, not an increase.

items.q: Increase 1200 by 30%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 30100 × 1200 = 360. New value = 1200 + 360 = 1560. 360 is the increase. 840 is a decrease of 30%.

items.q: Increase 45 kg by 20%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 20100 × 45 kg = 9 kg. New value = 45 kg + 9 kg = 54 kg. 9 kg is the increase. 36 kg is a decrease of 20%.

items.q: Increase 2.5 ℓ by 40%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 40100 × 2.5 ℓ = 1 ℓ. New value = 2.5 ℓ + 1 ℓ = 3.5 ℓ. 1 ℓ is the increase. 2.9 ℓ adds 0.4, not 40%.

items.q: A number increased from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 50 − 40 = 10. Percentage increase = 1040 × 100% = 25%. 20% divides by the new value (50). Always divide by the value before the change.

items.q: A number increased from 200 to 350. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 350 − 200 = 150. Percentage increase = 150200 × 100% = 75%. 150 is the increase, not a percentage. 175% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: A number increased from 30 to 60. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 60 − 30 = 30. Percentage increase = 3030 × 100% = 100%. 50% divides by the new value. The number doubled, so it went up by 100%.

items.q: A number increased from 800 to 920. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 920 − 800 = 120. Percentage increase = 120800 × 100% = 15%. 120 is the increase, not a percentage. 115% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: The price of a bicycle went up from $250 to $300. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = $300 − $250 = $50. Percentage increase = $50$250 × 100% = 20%. 16⅔% divides $50 by the new price ($300). $50 is not 50%.

items.q: The mass of a puppy increased from 2.5 kg to 3 kg. What is the percentage increase in its mass?
items.e: Increase = 3 kg − 2.5 kg = 0.5 kg. Percentage increase = 0.5 kg2.5 kg × 100% = 20%. 16⅔% divides by the new mass. 0.5 kg is the increase, not 0.5%.

items.q: After a 20% increase, the price of a school bag is $60. What was the price before the increase?
items.e: The price before is 100%. After the increase it is 120%. 120% → $60, 1% → 50¢, 100% → $50. $48 takes 20% of $60 away, but the 20% was of the old price, not of $60.

items.q: After a 25% increase, a library has 400 members. How many members did it have before the increase?
items.e: Before = 100%, after = 125%. 125% → 400, so 25% → 80 and 100% → 320. 300 takes 25% of 400 away, but the 25% was of the old number.

items.q: The number of visitors rose from 60 to 72. The new number is what percentage of the old number?
items.e: 7260 × 100% = 120%. 20% is the percentage increase. 83⅓% is the old number as a percentage of the new.

items.q: What is 35 increased by 100%?
items.e: 100% of 35 is 35. 35 + 35 = 70. An increase of 100% doubles the number. Do not add 100 or 1.

items.q: Which calculation gives 65 increased by 12%?
items.e: The new value is 100% + 12% = 112% of 65, so 65 × 112 ÷ 100 = 72.8. 65 × 12 ÷ 100 is only the increase. 65 × 88 ÷ 100 is a decrease.

items.q: The model shows the number of visitors to a museum before and after a change. All the units are equal. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Before = 5 units, after = 8 units. Increase = 3 units. 35 × 100% = 60%. 37.5% divides by the 8 units after. 3 units is not 3%.

items.q: A shop increased the price of a bag by 15%. The increase was $9. What is the new price of the bag?
items.e: 15% → $9, so 1% → 60¢ and 100% → $60 (the old price). New price = $60 + $9 = $69. $60 is the old price. $135 is $9 × 15.

items.q: The model shows 60 decreased by 20%. What is the new value?
items.e: 60 is 5 units, so 1 unit (20%) = 12. After the decrease there are 4 units: 48. 12 is only the decrease. Do not take away 20. 72 is an increase.

items.q: Decrease 90 by 30%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 30100 × 90 = 27. New value = 90 − 27 = 63. 27 is the decrease, not the new value. Do not take away 30.

items.q: Decrease $45 by 40%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 40100 × $45 = $18. New value = $45 − $18 = $27. $18 is the decrease. $63 is an increase.

items.q: Decrease 640 by 15%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 15100 × 640 = 96. New value = 640 − 96 = 544. 96 is the decrease. 736 is an increase. Do not take away 15.

items.q: Decrease 2 kg by 35%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 35100 × 2 kg = 0.7 kg. New value = 2 kg − 0.7 kg = 1.3 kg. 0.7 kg is the decrease. 1.65 kg takes away 0.35 kg, which is 35% of 1 kg, not of 2 kg.

items.q: Decrease 1500 by 8%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 8100 × 1500 = 120. New value = 1500 − 120 = 1380. 120 is the decrease. 1620 is an increase.

items.q: Decrease $3.60 by 25%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 25100 × $3.60 = 90¢. New value = $3.60 − 90¢ = $2.70. 90¢ is the decrease. $3.35 takes away 25¢, not 25%.

items.q: A number decreased from 50 to 40. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 50 − 40 = 10. Percentage decrease = 1050 × 100% = 20%. 25% divides by the new value (40). Always divide by the value before the change.

items.q: A number decreased from 80 to 50. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 80 − 50 = 30. Percentage decrease = 3080 × 100% = 37.5%. 60% divides by the new value (50). 30 is the decrease, not a percentage. 62.5% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: A number decreased from 60 to 30. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 60 − 30 = 30. Percentage decrease = 3060 × 100% = 50%. 100% divides by the new value (30). The number halved, so it went down by 50%.

items.q: The price of a fan was reduced from $120 to $90. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = $120 − $90 = $30. Percentage decrease = $30$120 × 100% = 25%. 33⅓% divides $30 by the new price ($90). $30 is not 30%. 75% is the new price as a percentage of the old.

items.q: The number of cars in a car park fell from 400 to 340. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 400 − 340 = 60. Percentage decrease = 60400 × 100% = 15%. 60 is the decrease, not a percentage. 85% is the cars left as a percentage of 400.

items.q: The water in a tank fell from 2.5 ℓ to 2 ℓ. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 2.5 ℓ − 2 ℓ = 0.5 ℓ. Percentage decrease = 0.5 ℓ2.5 ℓ × 100% = 20%. 25% divides by the new volume. 0.5 ℓ is the decrease, not 0.5%.

items.q: After a 20% discount, a pair of shoes costs $60. What was the price before the discount?
items.e: The price before is 100%. After 20% off, it is 80%. 80% → $60, 10% → $7.50, 100% → $75. $72 adds 20% of $60 back, but the 20% was of the price before, not of $60.

items.q: After a 15% decrease, a school has 340 students. How many students did it have before the decrease?
items.e: Before = 100%, after = 85%. 85% → 340, so 5% → 20 and 100% → 400. 391 adds 15% of 340, but the 15% was of the number before.

items.q: Which calculation gives 70 decreased by 15%?
items.e: The new value is 100% − 15% = 85% of 70, so 70 × 85 ÷ 100 = 59.5. 70 × 15 ÷ 100 is only the decrease. 70 × 115 ÷ 100 is an increase.

items.q: A price is reduced by 35%. The new price is what percentage of the old price?
items.e: The old price is 100%. 100% − 35% = 65%. 35% is the part taken off. 135% would be an increase.

items.q: The model shows the number of fish in a pond before and after some were sold. All the units are equal. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Before = 8 units, after = 6 units. Decrease = 2 units. 28 × 100% = 25%. 33⅓% divides by the 6 units after. 75% is the fish left.

items.q: The price of a lamp was reduced by 15%. The discount was $12. What is the new price of the lamp?
items.e: 15% → $12, so 5% → $4 and 100% → $80 (the price before). New price = $80 − $12 = $68. $80 is the price before. $92 adds the discount instead of taking it away.

items.q: Which is greater: 50 decreased by 20%, or 40 increased by 20%?
items.e: 50 decreased by 20%: 20% of 50 = 10, so 40. 40 increased by 20%: 20% of 40 = 8, so 48. 48 > 40, so 40 increased by 20% is greater. The same percentage gives different amounts when the starting values differ.

sets.title: PSLE-style word problems: discounts, before and after, units and parts

items.q: A pair of shoes was sold at a 20% discount. Siti paid $64 for it. What was the usual price of the shoes?
items.e: Usual price = 100% = 5 units. Siti paid 100% − 20% = 80% = 4 units. 4 units = $64, 1 unit = $16. 5 units = $80. $76.80 adds 20% of $64 back, but the discount was 20% of the usual price.

items.q: Mr Tan bought a television at a 15% discount. He saved $105. How much did he pay for the television?
items.e: 15% → $105, so 5% → $35 and 100% → $700 (the usual price). He paid $700 − $105 = $595. $700 is the usual price, not what he paid.

items.q: The number of students in a school increased by 8% this year. There are now 1350 students. How many students were there last year?
items.e: Last year = 100%. This year = 108%. 108% → 1350, 1% → 12.5, 100% → 1250. 1242 takes 8% of 1350 away, but the 8% was of last year’s number.

items.q: The number of students in a CCA increased from 48 to 60. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 60 − 48 = 12. Percentage increase = 1248 × 100% = 25%. 20% divides by the new number (60). 12 is the increase, not 12%.

items.q: Arjun spent 70% of his savings on a bicycle. He had $45 left. How much did the bicycle cost?
items.e: He had 30% left. 30% → $45, so 10% → $15. The bicycle cost 70% → 7 × $15 = $105. $150 is all his savings. $31.50 is 70% of $45, but the 70% is of his savings.

items.q: Ali has $75. Raju has $60. What percentage more money does Ali have than Raju?
items.e: Ali has $15 more. Compare with Raju’s money, because “more than Raju” means Raju is 100%. $15$60 × 100% = 25%. 20% divides by Ali’s money.

items.q: Ali has $75. Raju has $60. What percentage less money does Raju have than Ali?
items.e: Raju has $15 less. Compare with Ali’s money, because “less than Ali” means Ali is 100%. $15$75 × 100% = 20%. 25% divides by Raju’s money. 80% is Raju’s money as a percentage of Ali’s.

items.q: There were 600 students in a school. 40% of them were girls. Some more girls joined the school. Then 50% of the students were girls. How many girls joined the school?
items.e: Boys = 60% of 600 = 360. The number of boys did not change. After: boys = 50% = 360, so all the students = 720. Girls now = 720 − 360 = 360. Girls before = 240. Girls who joined = 360 − 240 = 120. 60 is only 10% of 600: the total also changed.

items.q: Jun Jie had 25% more stickers than Wei Ming. Jun Jie had 160 stickers. How many stickers did Wei Ming have?
items.e: “25% more than Wei Ming” means Wei Ming is 100% = 4 units and Jun Jie is 125% = 5 units. 5 units = 160, 1 unit = 32. Wei Ming = 4 units = 128. 120 takes 25% of 160 away, which is wrong.

items.q: Kavya’s height increased from 1.4 m to 1.47 m. What is the percentage increase in her height?
items.e: Increase = 1.47 m − 1.4 m = 0.07 m. 0.071.4 × 100% = 5%. 7% uses 7 cm as a percentage. 105% is her new height as a percentage of the old.

items.q: A bag cost $150. A shop gave a 20% discount. During a sale, it took a further 10% off the discounted price. What was the final price of the bag?
items.e: After 20% off: 80% of $150 = $120. After a further 10% off: 90% of $120 = $108. $105 takes 30% off $150, but the 10% is of $120, not of $150.

items.q: After a 35% discount, a bicycle cost $260. How much was the discount?
items.e: Paid 100% − 35% = 65%. 65% → $260, so 5% → $20. Discount = 35% → 7 × $20 = $140. $91 is 35% of $260, but the discount is 35% of the usual price. $400 is the usual price.

items.q: Mrs Lim had $800. She spent 25% of it on groceries and 40% of the remainder on clothes. How much money did she have left?
items.e: Groceries: 25% of $800 = $200. Remainder: $600. Clothes: 40% of $600 = $240. Left: $600 − $240 = $360. $280 takes 65% of $800, but the 40% is of the remainder, not of $800.

items.q: The price of durians was $20 per kg. In June the price increased by 20%. In July the new price decreased by 20%. What was the price per kg in July?
items.e: June: 120% of $20 = $24. July: 80% of $24 = $19.20. It is not $20: the 20% decrease is of $24, which is more than 20% of $20.

items.q: Mr Rahman put $5000 in a bank. The bank pays 2% interest per annum. How much money will he have in the bank after 1 year?
items.e: Interest = 2% of $5000 = $100. After 1 year: $5000 + $100 = $5100. $100 is only the interest. Do not add $2.

items.q: 2400 people visited the Singapore Zoo on Saturday. On Sunday, 15% fewer people visited. How many people visited the zoo on the two days altogether?
items.e: Sunday: 85% of 2400 = 2040. Altogether: 2400 + 2040 = 4440. 2040 is only Sunday. 2760 uses 15% more instead of fewer.

items.q: Ethan made a drink with syrup and water. 15% of the drink was syrup. He used 120 ml of syrup. How much water did he use?
items.e: 15% → 120 ml, so 5% → 40 ml and 100% → 800 ml of drink. Water = 800 ml − 120 ml = 680 ml. 800 ml is all the drink. 18 ml is 15% of 120 ml.

items.q: 40% of Siti’s money is equal to 60% of Nurul’s money. They have $150 altogether. How much money does Siti have?
items.e: 40% = 25 and 60% = 35. 25 of Siti’s money = 35 of Nurul’s money, so 2 × Siti’s money = 3 × Nurul’s money. Siti has 3 units and Nurul has 2 units (2 × 3 units = 3 × 2 units). 5 units = $150, 1 unit = $30. Siti = 3 units = $90. $60 is Nurul’s money.

items.q: There are 480 pupils in a school. 45% of them are boys. 25% of the girls are in the choir. How many girls are in the choir?
items.e: Girls = 55% of 480 = 264. Choir = 25% of 264 = 66. 54 is 25% of the boys. 120 is 25% of all the pupils. 198 is the girls not in the choir.

items.q: At a camp, the number of boys is 25% more than the number of girls. There are 36 more boys than girls. How many children are there at the camp altogether?
items.e: Girls = 100% = 4 units. Boys = 125% = 5 units. The difference is 1 unit = 36. Altogether = 9 units = 9 × 36 = 324. 180 is the number of boys and 144 is the number of girls.
